candidates.title: Directed behavior alignment with a hard pair-separation margin
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the frozen evaluation does not show higher pair-level ER while level-0 code usage is at least the control's, Gini is no higher than 0.216, prefix branches are at least 65.9, train-to-test frequency drift does not grow, sequence information does not fall, and Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 improve over the archived control. Also reject the pair-separation premise if behavior-pair codeword distances shrink materially.
candidates.risk: The assignment KL may be too weak to change hard assignments at the frozen weight, while increasing its effective influence may let the directed alignment overcome the separation barrier or distort the assignment distribution. Global repulsion may preserve geometric spacing without preserving occupancy balance, prefix branches, sequence information, or held-out recommendation quality.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The directed KL moves codewords to make the source assignment distribution predict the target assignment distribution. The per-pair hinge explicitly opposes any movement that brings the two selected codewords within delta; global repulsion also opposes codeword collisions. The separation barrier is not a guarantee that assignments never change or that the full training objective cannot overcome it; the measured test is whether pairwise codeword distances and exported usage remain preserved.

candidates.title: Directed soft assignment with balanced code capacity and pairwise codeword exclusion
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the frozen evaluation fails to raise pair-level ER while meeting the control-or-better constraints on level-0 code count, Gini, prefix branches, train-to-test frequency drift, and sequence information, or if Stage-3 recall@10 or NDCG@10 does not improve over control. A drop in hard code usage or a shrinkage in behavior-pair codeword distances also falsifies the intended safeguards.
candidates.risk: Uniform marginal capacity may improve global occupancy while disrupting behavior-relevant neighborhoods or prefix structure; the soft expected-distance constraint may be satisfied by spreading assignment probability without improving hard assignments. The directed cross-entropy may also be too weak to alter the frozen export, or may trade sequence information for a better pair match rate.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The directed cross-entropy moves codewords through the source and target soft assignments. The marginal capacity term pushes assignment mass toward equal code usage, while the expected-distance hinge pushes the endpoint assignment distributions away from codeword pairs that are too close. These terms oppose concentration and pair convergence, respectively, but do not mathematically guarantee unchanged hard-code occupancy or prefix structure.

candidates.title: Directed residual-geometry transport with codeword repulsion
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the frozen evaluation does not raise pair-level ER while preserving at least the control's level-0 code count, no-higher-than-control Gini, at least control-level prefix branches, no increase in train-to-test frequency drift, and no loss of sequence information, or if Stage-3 recall@10 and NDCG@10 fail to improve over control. Shrinking behavior-pair codeword distances would specifically falsify the claimed non-attractive residual interaction.
candidates.risk: The residual target may be poorly represented by the existing codebook geometry, causing broad codeword movement or harmful reassignment rather than a better partition. Global repulsion may prevent geometric collapse but cannot ensure that hard code usage, prefix branching, sequence information, or train-to-test stability are preserved; the residual may also be too noisy to improve held-out behavior-pair alignment.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The residual-geometry distribution moves codewords toward locations that represent the source-relative behavior residual, rather than directly pulling the source and target's current codewords together. Global repulsion opposes codeword collisions. This is not a hard constraint on the distance between a pair's assigned codewords, so pair convergence remains an explicit measured risk rather than a claimed impossibility.
